purpose: Six-view texture source for the shaman. Single-view projection reached only 16.5% observed coverage of the owned atlas; the other 83.5% was dilated invention, which is what the patchwork front view actually is. One photograph carries one side.

mesh_provenance.generator: hunyuan3d-dit-v2-mini-turbo, octree ladder 384:3000,320:2000,256:1500, 5 steps, seed 12345, conditioning 512x512
mesh_provenance.decimation: open3d quadric 1,112,498 -> 400,000 faces, 12.6 s, still watertight, 21 shells
mesh_provenance.unwrap: workers/unwrap_mesh_uv.py xatlas 2048; 4,611 charts, overlap 0.0, degenerate 0.019%, PROVEN
mesh_provenance.orientation: rotated +151.67 deg about Y to put the painted face at +Z (derived from the projection camera, not the silhouette), then +90 deg about X into the controls builder's Z-up basis; world_up in build_mvadapter_cpu_controls.py is hardcoded [0,0,1] and the first control build laid the figure on its side

camera_semantics.note: the tail-colour heuristic in audit_and_relabel_mvadapter_controls.py would have chosen raw 1 and put the skull face on the rear control; it counted 6448 vs 6559 orange pixels on a subject with no tail

oom_fallback.note: No 256 controls were built for this asset. A fallback would need its own control tensor and camera contract, so there is nothing to fall back to; an OOM here is a hard stop, not a retry.

prompt: high quality clean albedo reference of the same antlered bird-skull shaman, layered weathered cloth robes, bone staff with hanging pendants and charms, consistent materials, consistent identity, flat neutral lighting

repair_proofs.note: Both are hardware defects of this GTX 1660 SUPER, not asset-specific, so they carry over unchanged.

canonical_orientation.evidence: build_mvadapter_cpu_controls.py hardcodes world_up=[0,0,1]. The Y-up glTF build produced four horizontal views of a figure lying down, with the standing views landing in the top/bottom slots. Pre-rotating into Z-up fixed it; verified on the normal contact sheet.
